extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in category theory / algebraic topology (readers of a category-theory textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and formal development of monoids internal to a monoidal category: coherence theorem for monoidal categories, definition and basic properties of monoids and their actions, construction of free monoids, the simplicial category Δ and simplicial objects, and applications to (co)homology via comonads/resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence theorem / canonical maps between words
rubrics_metrics.description: For a monoidal category B, to each pair of words v, w of the same length n there is a unique natural isomorphism can_B(v,w): v_B → w_B (the canonical map) satisfying: the identity word/map is canonical; the identity transformation id_B, associator a (and its inverse), left and right unitors (and inverses), e and e^{-1} are canonical; composites and tensor-products of canonical maps are canonical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof constructs graphs G_n and G~ of words and basic arrows (instances of a, λ, ρ and their inverses and identities) and shows commutativity (uniqueness of composite) by induction and by using pentagon/triangle/naturality diamonds. This uniqueness allows defining a functor W→B sending the unique arrow between words to the unique composite in B; the coherence result guarantees canonical maps behave well under composition and tensoring. Use this when reducing parenthesization or moving unit inserts/omits: any diagram built from associators and unitors commutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a monoid in a monoidal category
rubrics_metrics.description: A monoid in a monoidal category (B, ⊗, e) is an object c ∈ B together with arrows μ: c⊗c → c and η: e → c such that the associativity and unit diagrams (the two displayed commutative diagrams) commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two commutative diagrams are the internal analogues of associativity and unit laws: μ∘(μ⊗id) = μ∘(id⊗μ) up to the associator, and μ∘(η⊗id) and μ∘(id⊗η) correspond to the identity via unitors. A morphism of monoids f: (c,μ,η) → (c',μ',η') is an arrow f:c→c' such that f∘μ = μ'∘(f⊗f) and f∘η = η'. Monoids in B form a category Mon B and there is a forgetful functor U: Mon B → B.

rubrics_metrics.name: General associative law for monoids (n-fold products equality)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a monoid (c, μ, η) any two n-fold products (parenthesizations) are equal via the canonical maps: for words v,w of same length, μ_v and μ_w satisfy μ_v = μ_w ∘ can_e(v,w).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define recursively the n-fold product maps μ_w. The proposition asserts compatibility of these iterated products with the canonical maps from the coherence theorem; the identity and unit cases are base steps and induction proceeds since canonical arrows are composites of associators and unitors. This legitimizes writing unambiguous 'n-fold product' independent of parenthesization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/construction of n-th ⊗-power (bn) and recursion
rubrics_metrics.description: For each b ∈ B define b^n (the n-th ⊗-power) by b^0 = e, b^1 = b, and b^{n+1} = (b^n) ⊗ b with all parentheses placed in front (left-associative convention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention fixes a canonical representative of each parenthesization class (used in the free-monoid construction). One may then define n-fold product maps p^{(n)}: c^{(n)} → c by recursion (p^{(0)} = η, p^{(1)} = id_c, p^{(n+1)} = μ ∘ (p^{(n)} ⊗ id)). Formula (7) expresses compatibility of these iterated products for sums of indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient conditions for existence of free monoids (left adjoint to forgetful functor)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B has countable (denumerable) coproducts and for each a ∈ B the functors a⊗- and -⊗a preserve these coproducts, then the forgetful functor U: Mon B → B has a left adjoint (free monoid on an object).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the free monoid on a as the coproduct ⨿_{n≥0} a^n with multiplication defined by juxtaposition using distributivity and canonical associativity isomorphisms; the coproduct injections supply the unit. Preservation of coproducts by tensoring ensures distributivity isomorphisms used in defining multiplication are isomorphisms. Check universality by building the unique monoid morphism out of universal properties of coproducts and iterated products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left (and right) actions of a monoid on an object
rubrics_metrics.description: A left action of a monoid (c, μ, η) on an object a ∈ B is an arrow ν: c⊗a → a such that the diagram expressing compatibility with μ and η (i.e., ν∘(μ⊗id) = ν∘(id⊗ν) up to associators and unitors, and ν∘(η⊗id)=id_a) commutes. Morphisms of actions are arrows f:a→a' commuting with actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions generalize module actions, and actions of monads on endofunctors. The category of left actions c-LAct has a forgetful functor to B which has a left adjoint sending b to c⊗b equipped with the obvious action. Right actions and bimodule-like commuting left-and-right actions are defined similarly. Use coequalizers to define tensor products over c when they exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: The simplicial category Δ (notations: A / .1) and its monoidal structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Δ has as objects finite ordinals n = {0,...,n-1} and arrows the weakly monotone functions. Ordinal addition + is a bifunctor making (Δ,+,0) a strict monoidal category. The object 1 is terminal and yields canonical arrows μ:2→1 and η:0→1 giving a universal monoid (1,μ,η) in Δ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every arrow in Δ can be expressed as iterated compositions and sums built from μ and η (general associative law holds). The universal property: for any monoid (c,μ',η') in a strict monoidal category (B,⊗,e) there is a unique monoidal functor F:Δ→B sending 1↦c and the generating μ,η to μ',η'. This characterizes Δ as the free strict monoidal category on one generator (the universal monoid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generators and relations presentation of Δ (face and degeneracy generators and relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Δ is generated by injective monotone maps b_i: n→n+1 and surjective monotone maps a_i: n+1→n (often denoted δ^i and σ^i) subject to relations: b_i b_j = b_{j+1} b_i (for i≤j), a_j a_i = a_i a_{j+1} (for i≤j), and a_j b_i = [cases depending on indices: identity or shifted generators] (relations (11),(12),(13) in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every arrow f:n→n' has a unique normal form as a composite of a string of a's then b's with monotonicity constraints on indices (canonical form (10)). These relations suffice to reduce any composite to that canonical form. This presentation underlies the simplicial identities for face and degeneracy maps in simplicial objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of simplicial object and simplicial identities
rubrics_metrics.description: A simplicial object S in X is a functor S:(Δ^+)^{op} → X, equivalently a sequence of objects S_n with face maps d_i: S_n→S_{n-1} (0≤i≤n) and degeneracy maps s_j: S_n→S_{n+1} (0≤j≤n-1) satisfying the simplicial identities (dual to relations (11)-(13)): d_i d_j = d_{j-1} d_i (i<j), s_j s_i = s_i s_{j+1} (i≤j), d_j s_i = [cases], etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augmented simplicial objects are extensions to degree -1 with augmentation B: S_0→S_{-1} satisfying B d_0 = B d_1. Given a simplicial object in an abelian category, define boundary maps ∂: S_{n+1}→S_n as the alternating sum ∑_{i=0}^{n+1} (-1)^i d_i to form a chain complex (∂∂=0) whose homology yields H_n(S). Use these identities to verify ∂^2=0 and to compute homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of an augmented simplicial object from a comonad (standard resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a comonad (L, ε, δ) on a category A, there is an associated augmented simplicial object with objects L^{n} (n-fold composite) and faces/degeneracies built from ε and δ (explicit formulas di = ε L^{n-i}, si = L^{i} δ L^{n-i-1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When A is abelian (or after applying a functor to an abelian category) the alternating-sum boundary maps yield a chain complex L_* a with augmentation to a. This complex is a (standard) resolution of a and may be used to compute derived functors (cohomology, etc.). This construction is the categorical origin of standard bar resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard free resolution for group (co)homology via comonad Z[G]⊗-
rubrics_metrics.description: For a group G, the comonad L = Z[G]⊗- on G-Mod produces a simplicial object whose n-chains are Z[G]^{⊗(n+1)} with explicit face maps d_i and degeneracies s_i given by the group-ring comultiplicative formulas; this yields the standard free resolution of the trivial G-module Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write tensors as x⊗x_1⊗...⊗x_n and apply the explicit formulas: d_0 removes the first factor by multiplication, interior d_i multiplies x_i and x_{i+1}, d_n drops the last factor, etc. Applying Hom_G(-,A) gives the cochain complex computing H^*(G,A); applying -⊗_G C computes H_*(G,C). Examples: H_0(G,Z)=Z, H_1(G,Z)=G/[G,G]. Use this resolution to compute group (co)homology and to relate cohomology classes to extensions and obstructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry / braided conditions for symmetric monoidal categories (beginning of closed categories section)
rubrics_metrics.description: A symmetric monoidal category is a monoidal category equipped with natural isomorphisms γ_{a,b}: a⊗b → b⊗a such that γ_{a,b}∘γ_{b,a} = id and compatibility diagrams with unitors and associator commute (the usual hexagon/triangle compatibility conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These natural isomorphisms enforce commutativity up to coherent isomorphism. The text begins the axioms: γ natural in a,b and the equations/diagrams (listed) must hold. Use these to transport structures (monoids, actions, etc.) between tensor factors and to simplify many coherence checks when symmetry is present.
